notes:
**Document and personal opening (134-2.146.note.document).** Author page 1 begins a French letter addressed “Cher Larry”, headed Villecun, “17/19 Juillet/juillet”, with 1975 on a separate line. The month’s case and a possible following point remain uncertain. Archive pencil foliation 146 is recorded only as a comment; H’s editorial note already gives both page numbers. The opening congratulates Larry on his daughter’s birth. The next paragraph asks about his nationality and academic status, interest in a position at Montpellier, and a possible visit to Montpellier or Villecun. These questions are reported, not answered or independently investigated.

**Mathematical discussion (134-2.146.claim.approach).** The author welcomes a response to his long letter and a constructive approach to the theory he foresees. He describes the proposed notion of a non-strict n-category and its nerve functor as a first precise approach, with the inserted merit “d’exister et”. He then criticises its technicality and lack of intuition. The comparison stops mid-sentence at “1-cat. et”, with an open parenthesis continued beyond this page. The words “que je prévois”, “certes”, and inserted “bien sûr” are retained as his qualifications; no construction, criticism or nerve property is proved or refuted in this transcription work.

**Ink decisions and slips (134-2.146.note.readings).** Each reader inspected the n in n-catégorie and numeral 1 in 1-cat.; neither was inferred from category-theoretic convention. The literal colon after position and the ending premièr are resolved without grammatical correction. The conditional ending remains serait/serais, and both sides of the physical line break show no joining hyphen before tu. The word after longue has a dot over i, without a circumflex, but its initial accent remains grave/acute. The strokes beneath cogitations and longue are continuous g descenders, not separate underlines. The disputed favoris/fantaisies remains uncertain. The cancelled phrase after pour has a tentative two-word reading, une structure; the cancelled adverb now retains naturellement first and évidemment second. Both deletion states are clear, while their letters remain among the least secure readings on the page. No expected French or mathematical wording was used to fill the cancellations.
